question: If ₹10,000 becomes ₹12,100 in 2 years at compound interest compounded annually, what is the annual percentage rate of compounding?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a 2-year compound interest period, the multiplying factor per year is the square root of the Amount to Principal ratio.

Ratio of A to P = 12100 ÷ 10000 = 121 ÷ 100

1-Year Multiplying factor = √(121 ÷ 100) = 11 ÷ 10

This means an interest of 1 unit is earned over a principal of 10 units in one year.

Rate of Interest (R) = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹10,000

Amount (A) = ₹12,100

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 ₹ 10,000
 Principal (P)
 
 
 ₹ 12,100
 Amount (A)
 
 
• 
 

 
 Time (T) = 2 Years
 Rate = R% p.a.
 
 Amount ÷ Principal = 12100 ÷ 10000 = 121/100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 12100 = 10000 × (1 + R/100)²

⇒ 12100 ÷ 10000 = (1 + R/100)²

⇒ 121 / 100 = (1 + R/100)²

⇒ √(121 / 100) = 1 + R/100

⇒ 11 / 10 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = (11 / 10) − 1

⇒ R/100 = 1 / 10

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for 2 Years CI

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years can be calculated as: Rₑff = 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%. For R = 10%, Rₑff = 20 + 1 = 21%.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a principal P is given by: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

3-Year Rate Shortcut

If the amount is given after 3 years, the 1-year multiplier is found by taking the cube root: ³√(A ÷ P).
